newsitem.title: UK: Royal Sun dips after in-line Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: Royal Sun dips after in-line Q1 results.

text.p: Shares in Royal & Sun Alliance Plc dipped in early trading on Tuesday after first-quarter results from the insurance group failed to provide any major positive surprise, dealers and analysts said.
The stock was down 5-1/2p at 484 by 0755 GMT in volume of 408,888 shares, extending a decline since the post-merger peak of 530p set on May 9.

Analysts said the company's UK performance was weak as expected, reflecting a huge increase in housing subsidence claims, and noted that the results were buoyed by a strong performance in the United States.
However views on the stock largely depend on assessments of the pace of progress in integrating the two firms' operations, analysts said.
Repeating a "hold" recommendation on the stock, analyst Tim Young at brokerage SocGen said the integration process may drag out longer than some expect.
"It is a huge task integrating the two groups and that makes us cautious for the short term," Young said. "I find it difficult to see how it can operate as a truly integrated unit before 1999."
At Lehman Brothers, analyst Rob Procter kept his "outperform" rating on the shares, arguing that good news on the integration progress should emerge through the next 12 months.

"They are likely to beat their cost savings targets and the share buyback could be the first of many," Procter said. Shareholders approved a buyback of up to five percent of its shares earlier this month.

Operating profit before tax rose 24 percent to 195 million stg in the three months ended March 31 from 157 million a year before, compared with analyst forecasts in a range between 170 million stg and 195 million.
The company said it had an "encouraging" start to the year with a strong performance in North America, adding that the integration process following last year's merger continued to timetable.
